title: Grateful Dead Live at The Strand Lyceum on 1972-05-26
lineage: TASCAM DA-20 (S/PDIF out) -> LynxTWO-B Audio Reference Interface (S/PDIF in) -> Wavelab 6.0 All editing and mastering on the GEMS Edit Station. Trac'ed Cdwave,Flac'ed TLH level 8

ai_review.summary: Excellent soundboard capture of a high‑energy 1972 London show featuring smoking Truckin’ > The Other One > Morning Dew and superb Keith/Garcia interplay.
ai_review.review: This recording delivers crystal‑clear, warm‑tube soundboard fidelity that lets the band’s ferocious four‑hour marathon shine. The night is highlighted by an epic Truckin’ → The Other One → Morning Dew suite, killer Pigpen organ work, and tight, soaring playing from Keith Godchaux and Jerry Garcia, while the first set rolls on for over two hours with strong performances throughout. Overall the show feels like a peak moment of the Europe ’72 tour.

ai_rating.rationale: The vast majority of detailed reviews award 4–5 stars, praising both the musical performance and the pristine soundboard recording; only a few outlier negative comments affect the average minimally.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp, balanced mix captured by Betty Cantor & Rex Jackson’s mobile 24‑track truck; warm tube‑amp character, no noticeable dropouts or major flaws.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Monstrous four‑hour set; first set >2 hrs with solid pacing, second set a seamless jam suite (Truckin’ → The Other One → Morning Dew) that keeps the energy soaring.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s tone is repeatedly praised (‘Jer‑tone’, ‘smoking guitar’) and his lock‑step interplay with Keith is highlighted as a show‑stopper.
band_member_comments.Phil: Solid bass work noted, including an intense brief solo before The Other One theme.
band_member_comments.Bob: Pigpen’s organ licks are called powerful and emotive; several reviewers note this being one of his last stellar performances.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith Godchaux receives high praise for fluid piano improvisation, extraordinary moments (even likened to Steve Winwood), and tight chemistry with Garcia.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill Kreutzmann’s percussion‑driven sections and drum solo within The Other One are highlighted as exceptional.
